Bug_Title: SING: Class using singleton design pattern has non-private constructor. (SING_SINGLETON_HAS_NONPRIVATE_CONSTRUCTOR)
Bug_Details:
This class is using singleton design pattern and has non-private constructor (please note that a default constructor might exist which is not private). Given that, it is possible to create a copy of the object, thus violating the singleton pattern.
The easier solution would be making the constructor private.
SEI CERT MSC07-J rule
Bug_Explanation: This class uses the Singleton pattern, which ensures that only one instance of the class is created. However, the constructor is not private, which allows for the creation of multiple instances. This violates the Singleton pattern.
Trigger_Explanation: The JUnit test created tries to create a new instance of SingletonExample by calling the non-private constructor directly. This violates the Singleton pattern and should trigger the bug.
